Playbook.name: Correlation — Possible BEC / Cloud-Account Compromise with Sensitive Data Loss - SOC Playbook

Reference.title: MITRE ATT and CK T1078 Valid Accounts
MITRE ATT and CK T1567 Exfiltration Over Web Service

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: This correlation fires when ONE account carries both a cloud-account-compromise indicator (Entra credential or privileged-role add, OAuth consent, mailbox forwarding or delegation, transport rule, anonymous SharePoint sharing) AND a sensitive-data-loss indicator (a High or Medium Microsoft Purview / DLP alert, or a bulk data-movement signal) within a short window. Triage question: is this a genuine Business Email Compromise where a compromised cloud identity is being used to move sensitive data, or are the constituent cloud alerts coincidental and individually benign?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: For a bank, a compromised M365 identity that is also tripping DLP (SWIFT, card, national-ID policies at JCB) is simultaneously account takeover, financial-fraud enablement and a reportable data breach. Confirmed cases require identity containment, IR and compliance notification.

Assets.AssetType: Microsoft 365 / Entra ID tenant (JCB) — mailboxes, SharePoint/OneDrive, Entra directory
Correlated across JCB Elastic Security detections on a shared account

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Elastic Security alerts index (.alerts-security.alerts-*) — verified live at JCB (4.1M alerts/30d). Fields used: kibana.alert.rule.name, kibana.alert.severity, kibana.alert.risk_score, user.name, source.ip, host.name, @timestamp. Correlation must rest on a SHARED ACCOUNT, not mere time-proximity.

M365 unified audit via Elastic Agent — verified live (8.1M docs/30d). JCB-specific facts: o365.audit.Operation is NOT populated at JCB (0 of 8.1M) — the operation is carried in event.action. The affected user of a Purview/DLP alert appears in o365.audit.ObjectId as an email (case varies, e.g. jcbank.com.jo vs JCBANK.COM.JO) — match case-insensitively. rule.name on those alerts is the DLP policy name.

O365 ingest lag is typically 20-60 min; all queries use a 4h window. norm_user referenced by the source rule is a computed field and is not stored on the alerts index — pivots here key on the stored user.name.

Signal.Name: Possible BEC / Cloud-Account Compromise with Sensitive Data Loss
Signal.Details: A cloud-compromise alert and a sensitive-data-loss alert are correlated on the same account within the window.

Input.name: $entity
Input.description: The correlated account as it appears on the alerts (user.name).

Input.name: $entity_email
Input.description: The same account's M365 UPN / primary email (matches o365.audit.ObjectId on DLP/compliance alerts).

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the full evidence story per the ClassificationGuidance — a real incident needs BOTH a compromise leg and a data-loss leg on the same account, not any single alert.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the alerts correlated on this account form a genuine BEC / cloud-account compromise with sensitive data loss, or a coincidental cluster of individually benign cloud alerts.

Step.name: List every alert that fired on this account
Step.Purpose: The set of distinct rules, severities and risk on the shared account shows whether a real multi-signal story exists (correlation by ACCOUNT, not time). Look for a compromise-leg rule and a data-loss-leg rule together.
Step.Query: FROM .alerts-security.alerts-* | WHERE user.name == "$entity" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS hits = COUNT(*), first_seen = MIN(@timestamp), last_seen = MAX(@timestamp), max_risk = MAX(kibana.alert.risk_score), severities = VALUES(kibana.alert.severity) BY kibana.alert.rule.name | SORT max_risk DESC | LIMIT 30
Step.AnalystNotes: A cloud-compromise rule (Entra credential/role add, OAuth consent, mailbox forwarding/delegation, transport rule, anonymous sharing) together with a data-loss rule (Purview/DLP, QA Office 365 High/Medium Severity) on the same account is the incident. A single low-fidelity rule repeating is not.

Step.name: Confirm the sensitive-data-loss leg in the M365 audit log
Step.Purpose: Pull the High/Medium Microsoft Security and Compliance (Purview/DLP) alerts for this account directly from the audit log — this is the data-loss evidence and names the policy that matched (e.g. SWIFT, card, national-ID).
Step.Query: FROM logs-o365.audit-* | WHERE @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours AND event.code IN ("SecurityComplianceAlerts","SecurityComplianceInsights") AND o365.audit.Severity IN ("High","Medium") AND TO_LOWER(o365.audit.ObjectId) == TO_LOWER("$entity_email") | KEEP @timestamp, o365.audit.Severity, rule.name, event.action, o365.audit.ObjectId, o365.audit.AlertId | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 25
Step.AnalystNotes: rule.name is the DLP/compliance policy. A High-severity SWIFT or card/national-ID policy match on the same account as a compromise indicator is a bank-grade data breach. No matching rows means the data-loss leg is not in M365 audit — the correlation may be resting on a non-M365 DLP source (Forcepoint) or is weaker.

Step.name: Confirm the cloud-account-compromise leg (mailbox / identity changes)
Step.Purpose: Identify persistence or takeover actions on or by this account — inbox rules, mailbox permission or delegation grants, transport rules, password or conditional-access changes, privileged group adds — the hallmarks of BEC.
Step.Query: FROM logs-o365.audit-* | WHERE @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours AND (TO_LOWER(user.name) == TO_LOWER("$entity") OR TO_LOWER(o365.audit.ObjectId) == TO_LOWER("$entity_email")) AND (event.action LIKE "*InboxRule*" OR event.action LIKE "Set-Mailbox*" OR event.action LIKE "Add-MailboxPermission" OR event.action LIKE "Add-RecipientPermission" OR event.action LIKE "*TransportRule*" OR event.action == "Change user password" OR event.action LIKE "Update PasswordProfile*" OR event.action LIKE "Set-ConditionalAccessPolicy" OR event.action LIKE "Add member to*") | KEEP @timestamp, event.action, user.name, o365.audit.ObjectId, source.ip | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 25
Step.AnalystNotes: A new external-forwarding inbox rule, a delegation grant or a transport rule alongside the DLP hit is a classic BEC exfil setup. If none appear, the compromise leg may be an Entra sign-in / OAuth signal instead — corroborate against INV-01 and INV-04.

Step.name: Where is the activity coming from
Step.Purpose: Summarise the source IPs seen across this account's alerts to spot an unfamiliar or external origin behind the correlated behaviour.
Step.Query: FROM .alerts-security.alerts-* | WHERE user.name == "$entity" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS alerts = COUNT(*), distinct_rules = COUNT_DISTINCT(kibana.alert.rule.name) BY source.ip | SORT alerts DESC | LIMIT 20
Step.AnalystNotes: JCB egress NAT is 94.249.88.0/24 — internal users appear from it. An external or unfamiliar source IP driving several distinct alert rules strengthens the compromise verdict.

Node.Condition: A cloud-account-compromise indicator (INV-01/INV-03: forwarding or delegation, transport rule, Entra credential/role/OAuth, anonymous sharing, password/CA change) AND a sensitive-data-loss indicator (INV-01/INV-02: High or Medium DLP/Purview policy match) on the SAME account within the window.
Node.Result: True Positive (BEC / Cloud-Account Compromise with Data Loss — contain identity, open IR, notify compliance)

Node.Condition: The constituent alerts are all authorised or proven-blocked — the DLP policy blocked the transfer and the "compromise" actions are an approved admin/change ticket for this account.
The correlation is inflated by a known-noisy constituent rule pending tuning, or by an identity-mapping quirk (norm_user collision) — no genuine compromise+data-loss pairing exists.
Node.Result: Misconfiguration (tune the constituent rule / correlation join)

Node.Condition: A real compromise-and-data-loss pairing is plausible but the scope, the actor or the data sensitivity cannot be confirmed from telemetry alone.

FalsePositive.Definition: The correlated alerts are individually authorised or proven-blocked: an approved admin change on the account plus a DLP event that the policy blocked, with no compromise.

Indicators.Item: DLP alert shows the transfer was blocked, and the recipient/context is legitimate business.
The identity/mailbox change maps to an approved change ticket and a recognised admin.
Source IP is JCB egress NAT 94.249.88.0/24 and the account's behaviour is otherwise normal.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm each constituent alert is authorised or blocked; document the tickets/owners; close as false_positive.

TruePositive.Definition: A compromised M365 identity is being used to move sensitive data — a BEC / cloud-account compromise with data loss.

Indicators.Item: Compromise leg (forwarding/delegation/transport rule/OAuth/role add) and data-loss leg (High/Medium DLP policy match) on the same account.
Related timing and an unfamiliar or external source IP.
DLP policy touches regulated data (SWIFT, card, national ID).

SOCAction.Item: Contain the identity: disable/reset the account, revoke sessions and refresh tokens, remove attacker inbox rules / delegations / transport rules.
Open IR; reconstruct the chain from the constituent alerts; scope what data left and notify compliance.

Misconfiguration.Definition: A known-noisy constituent rule or an identity-join quirk inflated the correlation with no genuine multi-stage story.

Indicators.Item: One constituent rule is a high-volume low-fidelity signal pending tuning.
The paired alerts belong to different real people mapped to one norm_user.

SOCAction.Item: Tune the noisy constituent rule or correct the correlation join; re-evaluate; document.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Review the constituent alerts (INV-01); confirm a compromise leg and a data-loss leg on the same account.
If confirmed, contain the identity: disable the account, revoke sessions and refresh tokens.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Remove attacker persistence: external-forwarding and inbox rules, mailbox FullAccess/SendAs delegations, malicious transport rules, illicit OAuth grants.
Reconstruct the exfil path from INV-02/INV-03; scope the sensitive data exposed; open formal IR.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Restore the account under new credentials and MFA; enforce conditional access; tighten admin-consent and privileged-role governance (PIM).
Tune noisy constituent rules to sharpen correlation fidelity; complete compliance/breach notification as required.

Escalation.Trigger: Confirmed compromise-plus-data-loss pairing, a regulated-data DLP policy match (SWIFT/card/national ID), or unconfirmed scope of what data left.

FalsePositiveClosure.Item: Every constituent alert confirmed authorised or proven-blocked; tickets/owners documented; no compromise.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Identity contained and restored; attacker persistence removed; exfil chain reconstructed; data exposure scoped and compliance notified.
